lines.text: Bread is fluffy because bakers pump air in.
Yeast. Billions of tiny living cells. Add flour and water, and they start eating the sugar.
Every bite, they burp out carbon dioxide gas. Plus a little alcohol.
Calm down. Kneading links two flour proteins into gluten. A stretchy net, like bubble gum.
The net traps the burps, so the dough puffs up like a thousand tiny balloons.
Then why bake it? Just eat the balloon.
Because it's raw. In the oven, the gas swells one last time. Bakers call it oven spring.
Around one-forty, the yeast die. The gluten and starch set, and the bubbles freeze in place.
So every hole in my toast is a frozen burp.
Yep. And most of the alcohol bakes off. That's part of the smell. And now you know.
I still think they pump it.
